status: PROVISIONAL — the dates marked verified come from the cited public sources; every tier, window, fragment rule and sector mapping is our hypothesis (Raul accepted them as hypotheses on 2026-11-23). Nothing here is sent to Meta and nothing is stored: it only splits the owner's monthly cap across the weeks of a month.
source: m-25091392 part 1; dates researched 2026-11-23 (docs/calendario-plan-del-mes.md); Raul's answers of 2026-11-23: amounts rounded like investment_profile.py, levels 1.0/1.25/1.5 as hypotheses, dates filtered by the 8 Brand Kit sectors, no regional dates (Carnaval de Barranquilla and Norte de Santander's Mother's Day left out), Halloween added for CO.
update_notes: Resolved for 2026-12 → 2027-12. Rules by weekday, fixed day, day of month or Easter keep working for later years; the entries with exact start/end dates (Hot Sale, CyberLunes, school start) are announced each year and are updated BY HAND every December, with a new version when a tier, window or mapping changes.
tiers_source: hypothesis (Raul, 2026-11-23): three levels; a week takes the highest level of its dates, never multiplied; a week's weight = its days in the month × level
window_source: hypothesis: people buy the gift before the date; the week holding a grande date and the weeks holding any of the 10 days before it get the grande level
merge_source: hypothesis: a Monday–Sunday week cut by the month to 3 days or fewer at the start or the end joins its neighbour, so the card shows 4 or 5 rows
rounding_source: Raul, 2026-11-23: each week rounded down with investment_profile.py's display step (COP to $1.000, other currencies to the whole unit); the remainder goes to the heaviest week (the first on a tie) so the weeks add up exactly to the cap
sector_groups_source: hypothesis: which of the 8 Brand Kit sectors (discovery_seed.NICHE_LABELS) sell around each kind of date; a business with no sector gets every date
rules_source: rule forms: dates [MM-DD]; month + weekday + nth (-1 = last) + offset_days; days_of_month (clamped to the month's last day); first_business_days (Monday–Friday, holidays ignored); easter_offset_days; start + end (exact, one year). length_days (default 1) turns a single day into a range.
